turns.t: Good morning, Doctor. I do apologise for taking up your time, but I have been left with sore ribs since a dreadful bout last week.
Morning. No need to apologise. Which side is it, and when exactly did it start?
The right side, low down towards the back. It began one week ago, quite suddenly, in the middle of a coughing fit.
Right. Does anything make it worse?
Yes, when I cough, and also a deep breath. Laughing is rather out of the question at the moment.
Is it a sharp pain or more of an ache?
Sharp, I would say, but only at those moments. In between it is a dull soreness. Moderate overall, though it does keep me awake if I roll onto that side.
Fair enough. Are you coughing up any blood?
No, nothing like that, thank goodness.
Good. And are you short of breath at rest, or going upstairs?
No, not at all. My breathing seems perfectly all right, it is only the pain that catches me.
Have you taken anything for it?
I haven't, I am afraid. I am not fond of tablets. I only take amlodipine, 5 mg every morning, and I have not changed that.
Fine, carry on with that. Any allergies I should write down before we go further?
No, none that I am aware of. I have never had a reaction to anything.
Good. Have you had any operations in the past?
Just the one. I had my appendix removed about twelve years ago, and it all went smoothly.
Thanks. And do you smoke, or have you ever?
I gave up smoking in my fifties. It was the best decision I ever made, if I may say so.
Well done. Right, I'll take a few readings so I have a baseline.
Your pulse is 76 beats per minute, and your oxygen saturation is 98 percent.
Is that satisfactory?
Perfectly. Temperature is 36.8 degrees Celsius too. So nothing there that worries me.
That is a relief. My daughter was convinced I had done something terrible to myself.
Let me lay out the options. We can wait and see, we can get a picture, or we can do both. I'd like to arrange a chest X-ray today.
Would that be necessary? I should not like to waste anyone's resources.
It's not a waste. After a hard cough, a picture settles the question, and then we can plan properly.
In that case, certainly. Where do I go for it?
Radiology is down the corridor on the left. Reception will give you a form, and it's usually quick.
Splendid. And in the meantime, is there anything I ought to be doing?
Yes. Hug a pillow against your side when you cough, and keep walking gently. Resting completely tends to make it stiffer.
A pillow. I would not have thought of that.
Try short, shallow breaths first, then build up to a few slow deep ones every hour or so.
Every hour, understood. Shall I come back to see you afterwards?
Yes, let's see you again in two weeks, and we'll go over how it's settling and what the picture showed.
In two weeks. I shall ask the receptionist to book it.
Good idea. She'll find a slot for you on your way out.
And if the pain gets worse before then?
Ring the surgery straight away. Don't sit on it.
I will not. Thank you very much indeed, Doctor.
You're welcome. Mind the corridor floor, it's just been washed.
Thank you. Goodbye.
Goodbye.

chief_complaint.value: sore ribs since a dreadful bout last week

clinical_actions.description: Hug a pillow when coughing, keep walking gently, practise slow deep breaths hourly
